---
title: smalldocs 0.2.0
subtitle: Themes from git repositories, and notes in the margin
date: 2026-10-16
author: Rahul Dave
categories: [release]
image: ../images/mark.svg
---

A site can now use a theme from a git repository. `smalldocs add org/repo` copies the theme into the
folder `_extensions/` of the project, and `theme: <name>` uses it. The same folder can hold a theme for
Quarto, so one repository serves both tools. `smalldocs themes` lists the themes and where each came
from. See [Themes](../guide/themes.qmd#a-theme-from-a-git-repository).

[smalldocs-tufte](https://github.com/rahuldave/smalldocs-tufte) is the first such theme. It gives a
site the look of Tufte CSS, in a light mode and a dark mode. Its
[demo](https://rahuldave.com/smalldocs-tufte/) shows it.

A page can now put content in the margin, as Quarto does:

- `reference-location: margin` puts each footnote beside the paragraph that cites it.
- A div with the class `.column-margin`, or a span with the class `.aside`, goes in the margin.
- `fig-cap-location: margin` puts the caption of a figure beside it.
- The classes `.column-page`, `.column-screen` and `.column-body-outset` make content wider than the
  text.

See [The margin and wide content](../guide/markdown.qmd#the-margin-and-wide-content).

Other changes:

- A site with a light theme and a dark theme starts in the mode that the browser prefers. The page
  loads the right theme before it shows anything, so it does not flash the other theme first.
- A theme file named `x.min.css` keeps its name in the site.
- A theme can set the size of the text with the variable `--sd-root-font-size`.
- In a `_quarto.yml`, `format: <name>-html` is read as `html`.
